title: Choose a response before uncertainty becomes motion
description: Inject a runtime fault, select an independent monitor, and assign a fallback. The response must fit the hazard window and reduce residual risk without pretending that task throughput is safety.
modelNote: Risk scores are comparative teaching values. A real safety case requires hazard analysis, verified hardware behavior, and evidence for the specific robot application.

failures.label: Primary camera occluded
failures.detail: The policy still has proprioception, but the scene estimate is stale and incomplete.
failures.safeState: Hold position and reacquire a valid scene

failures.label: Unexpected contact force
failures.detail: The wrist sensor reports a force spike during a grasp near a person.
failures.safeState: Remove drive torque and release stored energy

failures.label: Remote policy unavailable
failures.detail: Commands and model responses stop arriving while the robot is moving.

failures.label: Localization disagreement
failures.detail: Wheel odometry and visual localization disagree near a restricted zone.
failures.safeState: Stop before the geofence and request recovery

monitors.label: Policy self-check
monitors.detail: The learned policy reports its own confidence and anomaly score.

monitors.label: Independent runtime supervisor
monitors.detail: Separate sensor-health, geofence, force, and freshness rules watch the proposal.

monitors.label: Hardware safety channel
monitors.detail: Certified limits observe a narrow set of physical hazards without model inference.

fallbacks.label: Continue the proposal
fallbacks.detail: Preserve full capability and trust the current plan.

fallbacks.label: Limited-motion controller
fallbacks.detail: Reduce speed and force, keep only local sensing, and attempt one reversible action.

fallbacks.label: Controlled stop
fallbacks.detail: Cancel model authority and transition to the application-defined safe state.

fallbacks.label: Remote teleoperation
fallbacks.detail: Pause autonomous motion until an operator accepts control with a verified view.
